text:
Liam: DeployBot fired an auto-rollback on prod-canary for v4.0.0 -> reason shows "error-rate surge". I see a DB migration running in parallel. hold on ordering?
DeployBot: [auto-rollback initiated] Reason: 1.2% errors over 2m on canary, p50/p95 stable. Action: rollback to v3.13.4 in 2m unless manual override.
Priya (release): wait - we scheduled a compatibility migration this window. if migration is the cause, rollback could leave half-migrated state for some jobs. we need a quick check.
Nina (runtime): confirmed there	was a migration job kicked off by infra at 6171239800. logs show lock contention spikes. error type is 503-ish transient. not sure model change is root cause.
Maya Ops: risk assessment: if we rollback while migration mid-flight, some queued workers may reprocess and double-run. prefer to pause traffic and coordinate with infra.
Liam: options: (A) allow auto-rollback (fast) (B) pause canary traffic entirely and drain, resume migration (C) manual rollback + pinned release + comms. Thoughts?
Support: customer impact: 2 support pings, both background jobs failing intermittently. no customer-facing UI errors yet.
Priya (release): prefer B for now: pause canary (0% traffic), then wait for migration to finish, then resume canary on v4.0.0 once infra confirms. that avoids rollback churn.
DeployBot: manual override available. Use `deployctl override --id 6171239876 --action hold` to stop auto-rollback.
Nina (runtime): if we hold, I'll enable verbose tracing for the canary fleet and increase sampling to 20% for 10m. that's needed to separate DB vs model signals.
Maya Ops: who will run the hold? I can. once held, I'll post a maintenance banner and notify infra.
Liam: go ahead Maya. Priya, prep a short internal blurb so support & SRE have a uniform message.
Maya Ops: running `deployctl override --id 6171239876 --action hold` now. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Maya Ops: hold confirmed. canary traffic set to 0%. banner set: "Investigating background job failures on canary; pausing canary traffic while we investigate."
Priya (release): posting internal note: "Canary v4.0.0 paused. Observed increase in background job errors correlating with infra DB migration. No rollback executed. We'll resume or rollback after telemetry review."
Nina (runtime): traces indicate retries and deadlocks in migration window; after retries errors drop. p95 unchanged. leaning infra as cause.
DeployBot: auto-rollback canceled by hold. No rollback performed.
Liam: infra team status?
Support: infra confirmed migration completed at 6171239930. post-migration error rate back to baseline for non-canary traffic.
Nina (runtime): re-enabling canary traffic slowly to 5% with monitoring rules. using fast ramp 1->5 over 2m. if errors exceed 0.8% revert to 0 immediately.
Maya Ops: executing `deployctl promote --target-tag v4.0.0 --scope canary --traffic 5%` now.
Maya Ops: traffic at 5%. monitoring.
DeployBot: note: ramp policy in effect. will auto-rollback if errors > 0.8% for 3 consecutive minutes.
Liam: 90s in, metrics look stable. p95 still nominal.
Support: support tickets updated, customers notified with the message Priya drafted.
Priya (release): I'll publish a short note in #release-notes: "Canary paused during DB migration; resumed. No rollback required. Continuing observation."
Nina (runtime): increasing sampling done; no systemic model regressions observed. closing loop in 20m and then mark canary as healthy if stable.
Liam: thanks team. big call: prefer prevent noisy auto-rollback during infra ops. follow-up: add migration lock detection to DeployBot to reduce false positives. @DeployBot ops triage ticket?
Priya (release): filing a tiny postmortem and a DeployBot enhancement issue. assigning to runtime + infra.
DeployBot: acknowledged: created issue RB-2026 for migration-aware rollback gating.
Liam: thread resolved, reopening only if errors reappear."
